column2: Griha-kshata, Dandadhara, Gandharva, Bhringaraja, Mriga, Pitri-gana-adhisha, then Dauvarika (Dvarapala),
Sugriva, Surya, Aditi and Diti — these are the thirty-two gods. Then four stand at the north-east and other corners, near them:
Apa, Savitra, Jaya and Rudra in order. Alternately the east and others are remembered around Brahma:
Aryaman, Savita, Vivasvan, Vibudhadhipa, Mitra, Rajayakshman, and Prithvidhara, and the eighth Apavatsa.
These are the forty-five gods: Apa, Apavatsa, Parjanya, Agni, Diti in order (among those of the corners).
This is the group belonging to the directions; so too in all the corners. Twenty of them are outside, and these always have two parts.
Aryaman, Vivasvan, Mitra and Prithvidhara, around Brahma in the four directions, are remembered as having three parts.
The knower of Vastu should worship Brahma and the gods of one, two and three parts with the Vastu mantra, with durva, curd, rice-grains and the like.
Or with the Brahma mantra, he should give a pair of white cloths, and all the services of invocation and so on in order.
He should offer food of three kinds with instruments, and then betel. Then the doer should pray to the Vastu-Person:
Homage to you, O Vastu-Purusha, devoted to the earth-bed, O Lord; always make my house rich in wealth, grain and the like.
Having so prayed, he should give a fee to the officiant as able, and before him feed Brahmins according to his ability.
The man who rightly performs Vastu worship by this method obtains health, sons, wealth and grain.
One who enters a new house without Vastu worship suffers diseases and many troubles, and every calamity.
He should not enter a house without doors, without a roof, or without offerings of food; it is a mine of misfortunes.
Now the journey of kings and others, for the success of desired aims, I shall tell for those whose birth is known well.
For men whose birth is unknown, gain of fruit is like (accidental) letters shaped by worm-eaten wood; for them too the rise of fruit comes by the question, rising sign, omens and the like.
A journey on the sixth, eighth, twelfth, empty tithis, new moon and full moon, or on the first of the bright half, brings poverty and ruin.
Under Anuradha, Punarvasu, Mrigashira, Hasta, Revati, Ashvini, Pushya and Dhanishta, not the seventh, fifth or third ones: journeys give the desired fruit.
One should not go east on Saturday or Monday, south on Thursday, west on Venus's day or Sunday, north on Mercury's day or Mars's.
The stars named after Indra, Aja, Pada, Chaturasya, Aryaman are "spears" in the east; all-door stars are Mitra, Arka, Jiva, Ashvini...
In order, the stars for each direction's door are seven and seven from the fire-star (Krittika). One should not cross the Parigha line; not go toward the fire or wind direction.
The south-east is by the stars of the east, and so the intermediate directions likewise; the signs of the directions, Aries and the rest, repeat in order.
When the lord of the direction is on the forehead, the traveller does not return. The Sun in the ascendant is the forehead for the east.
Venus in the twelfth or eleventh is the forehead for the south-east; Mars in the tenth, from the ascendant, for the traveller...
Rahu in the ninth or eighth is the forehead for the south-west; Saturn in the seventh from the ascendant is the forehead for the west.
The Moon in the sixth or fifth is the forehead for the north-west; Mercury in the fourth is the forehead for the north.
Jupiter in the second or third is the forehead for the north-east. The man wishing to live should leave the forehead (direction) and go.
If a planet in reverse (vilomaga) is near the ascendant of the journey, it brings defeat to the king; and his group, even if in the ascendant.
Journeys favourable to the Sun's and Moon's paths give good fruit; in their absence, by day or night; otherwise death for the traveller.
With Venus combust, loss of the undertaking; with Venus opposed (pratishukra), defeat; the planets cannot remove the fault made by pratishukra.
For the five gotras Vasishtha, Kashyapa, Atri, Bharadvaja and Gautama, there is no pratishukra.
In marriage within one village, in famine, in war of kings, in disturbance of Brahmins or of kings, there is no pratishukra.
Venus in debilitation, in an enemy's house, retrograde, or defeated gives defeat to the traveller; if exalted, victory.
If in one's own eighth house or ascendant, or desired sign, or in the eighth from an enemy, or in the sign of their lord, death for the traveller, without doubt.
When the lords of the birth-sign, the eighth and the ascendant are mutually friends, the faults arising from the birth sign and the eighth star are destroyed.
Aspected or joined by cruel planets, even a dual sign gives defeat; in a journey, a fixed rising is not desired, with benefits aspecting by itself.
In the five stars from Dhanishta's half, collecting grass and wood, going south, bed, and keeping the house secret should not be done.
At the birth-rising or birth-star, or the star of their lord, or the Indra-house: for the traveller there will be destruction of enemies.
With a head-rising in the ascendant, or an ascendant in a direction, or a benefic sign in the ascendant: then the traveller destroys enemies.
At the enemy's birth-rising, birth-sign or the eighth rising, or in the sign where their lord stands: the traveller destroys enemies.
The road is crooked with Pisces rising or the Pisces division; for all journeys the pot-rising or pot-division is condemned.
A water ascendant or water division is auspicious for water-born; the twelve houses (bhavas) are: body, treasury, archer (third), vehicle, counsel,
enemy-path, life, mental work, gain and non-gain — twelve houses by rising.
Cruel planets destroy the houses, especially the Sun and Mars; they do not destroy action; benefics nourish except the enemy.
Venus does not nourish the seventh and the body, nor the Moon death. Leaving off travel to the south in all quarters, travellers —
this Abhijit moment-yoga gives success of desired fruit; even on a day lacking purity of the five limbs it gives fruit.
The yogas for journeys are various; I shall tell those from place to place; success of fruit comes for kings from the yoga ascendant, for Brahmins from the star.
For others by the strength of the muhurta, and for thieves by omens. A yoga is Venus, Mercury or Jupiter by one in a centre or trine.
Adhiyoga is by two; yoga-adhiyoga by three. With yoga, safety for travellers; with adhiyoga, victory.
With yoga-adhiyoga, safety, victory and prosperity; with the Moon, Saturn and the Sun in the houses of action, enemy and body,
for the king who has gone to battle victory-Lakshmi is certain. With Venus, Sun, Mercury, Saturn and Mars in the ascendant and third and enemy houses...
the foe in front of the traveller melts like lac in fire. With Jupiter in the ascendant, and other planets in the second and eleventh,
the king who has gone is led by the enemy's army to Yama's house. With Venus in the ascendant, the Sun in the eleventh, the Moon in the fourth,
the king who has gone kills enemies like a lion a herd of elephants. With Venus exalted in the ascendant and the Moon exalted in the eleventh,
the king kills the troubled enemies as Keshava killed Putana. With benefics in the trine and centre, and malefics in the third, eleventh and sixth,
misfortune goes to the traveller as a woman going to meet her lover. With Jupiter, Sun, Moon in the ascendant, sixth and eighth,
the enemy army before him is unsteady like a wicked man's friendship. With Saturn and Mars strong in the third, tenth and eleventh, and benefics,
the enemy's earth is in the hand of the king who journeys. With Jupiter exalted in the ascendant and the Moon in the eleventh,
the king who goes kills enemies as Pinaka-bearer did Tripura. With Venus rising at the head in the ascendant and Jupiter in the eleventh,
the king who goes kills enemies as Kumara did Taraka. With Jupiter in the ascendant, Venus in a centre or in a trine,
the king who goes burns enemies as fire burns a forest. With Mercury in the ascendant, benefics in a centre, and the star of the lineage...
kings dry up enemies as the sun's rays dry a pool in summer. With a benefic in the trine, centre, and the Moon in the eleventh, or the Sun,
the king who goes kills enemies as the sun darkness. With benefics in their own house, centres and trines,
the king destroys enemies as fire a grass-heap. With the Moon well-placed and Jupiter in a centre, a mantra with Om is the king who goes
who kills all enemies as the five-syllable mantra kills sins. With Venus in "vargottama" and in this very ascendant,
the king who goes kills enemies as remembrance of Hari kills floods of sins. With benefics in a centre or trine and the Moon in vargottama,
he kills even kinsmen and enemy kings, as one who splits the kin. With Jupiter in a friend's house in a centre, or Venus in a trine,
the king who goes kills enemies as Garuda serpents. With benefics in centre or trine and in vargottama,
the king destroys enemies as the Ganga sins. Kings who go to conquer enemies — by these yogas called "kings",
the fire of anger is quenched by drops of tears of the enemy's women. On the tenth of the waning fortnight (loss-of-strength) in the month is called Vijaya.
There for travellers victory is certain, or at least no defeat. But above omens the chief is the mind's rising.
Therefore for the resolute the cause of fruit is the mind's rising by effort. When festival, thread-ceremony, marriage, installation, impurity of birth or death is unfinished,
a mortal wishing to live should not travel. At a fight of buffalo and rat, in a domestic quarrel, in the fertile season,
if clothes slip, in anger, or at an evil word, the king should not go. Ghee-rice, sesame-flour rice, fish rice, ghee milk-rice,
having eaten in order from the east, the king goes and conquers enemies. Sajjika, milk-rice, sour gruel, milk, curd,
milk, sesame-rice: having eaten on Sunday and other days in order; kulmasha, sesame-rice, curd, honey, ghee, milk,
deer meat and its essence, milk-rice, bird, deer, hare meat, shashtika rice, priyangu cakes,
the flesh of various egg-born, tortoise, porcupine, iguana, hare; havishya, kricara, mung rice, barley cake,
fish rice, variegated rice, curd rice in order from Ashvini: having eaten, the king goes with elephants, horses, chariots and men, and conquers enemies.
He should offer sesame in the fire and worship the lord of the direction; bowing to gods and Brahmins with their blessings, the king goes.
With colour, cloth, perfume and the like of each, by his mantra as laid down: Indra on Airavata, shining with Shachi,
thunderbolt in hand, golden, adorned with divine ornaments; Agni seven-handed, seven-tongued, six-faced, riding a ram,
dear to Svaha, red, bearing ladle, spoon and weapon; Yama with the staff weapon, red-eyed, riding a buffalo,
dark, with red ones, facing upward, auspicious; Nirriti, blue, holding sword and shield, with long nails,
with upright hair, misshapen eyes, long neck, lord; Varuna with the serpent noose, yellow, riding a crocodile,
husband of Kalika, adorned with jewelled ornaments, the form of life of beings, two-armed, staff in hand;
Vayu riding a black antelope, one should worship, husband of Anjana; Kubera on a horse, pot in hand, two-armed, golden,
lord of Chitralekha, leader of Yakshas and Gandharvas; Pinaka-bearer on a bull, Gauri's lord, unsurpassed,
white, moon-crested, with a serpent as sacred thread. If the king is not himself to go, by observation it should be done by others for him.
The departure, umbrella, banner, weapons and vehicles: from his own place the place of departure is two hundred staffs (lengths)
or forty or twelve; he has himself gone out. He should not stay in one place for more days, or seven or eight.
He should go five nights ahead, and again in another ascendant. The king should not go in unseasonal lightning, thunder or rain,
nor in the three kinds of portents, for seven nights. Omens: the cries of the ... jackal, crow, dove (on the left side).
Cries of the bird jhajha, ibhuk, khema, and cow, going on the left side; the yellow-mouthed bird and Bharadvaja bird: going on the right.
Except the blue jay, quadrupeds on the left are held auspicious; except a black one; in journey, sight of the blackbird is...
Boar, hare, iguana, and mention of snakes are auspicious. Seeing something stolen is not desired; sight of monkeys or bears...
Peacock, goat, mongoose, blue jay and dove are auspicious by mere sight on a journey; reversed on entering.
Success of journey occurs on seeing, except a corpse; on entering, a weeping corpse or giving corpse...
Outcastes, eunuchs, matted-locks, the intoxicated, the vomiting, those with medicines, those anointed with fat, bone, skin, charcoal, wood, the diseased,
jaggery, cotton, salt, enemy-questions, grass, snakes, barren women, hunchbacks, red-robed ones, loose-haired, the hungry —
seen by naked ones at the time of departure, success does not occur. Blazing fires, good horses, thrones of kings, city women,
perfume, flowers, rice, umbrella, chowries, palanquin; the king (seeing) edibles, sugar-cane, fruit, clay, bathing-water, honey, ghee, curd, cow...
liquor, meat, nectar-washed cloth, conch, bull-banner; auspicious women, full pots, jewels, water-vessel, cow, Brahmin,
kettledrum, mridanga, tabor, bell, lute sounds, Vedic auspicious chanting — these give success of work to travellers.
If at first an adverse omen is seen, the traveller should remember his chosen deity; at the second, he should worship Brahmins and return.
A sneeze in all directions is not desired; a cow's sneeze gives death; what is done by children, the old, the sick or the nasal is fruitless.
Another's wife, a Brahmin's or god's property: he should not touch there elephants, horses of the directions. Having reached the enemy city, he should not kill women or the weaponless.
The new house-entering should first be done in the northern course; on the previous day having done the Vastu worship and offering.
In the months Magha, Phalguna, Vaishakha, Jyeshtha it is good; entering is middling in Margashirsha and Kartika.
Entering is auspicious under the stars Shatabhisha... Varuna, Tvashtra, Mitra and the fixed stars, when Jupiter and Venus are visible.
On days other than Mars's and on tithis other than empty ones and new moon, entering by day or night gives auspiciousness.
With strength of Moon and star, in the forenoon, on a good day, in a fixed rising and fixed division, with the eighth pure,
with benefics in trine and centre, and others in the third, eleventh and sixth, with the Moon not in the twelfth, eighth or sixth from the ascendant,
in the doer's birth-star or ascendant, or in their upachaya houses, the entering ascendant gives prosperity; in other stars grief and poverty.
Having made the lovely house visible with proper auspicious sounds, the wise man should enter with the sun on his left and the water-vessel in front.
(Rain omens:) At the year's start, with the Moon in a watery sign or in a centre in the bright half, heavy rain with benefics aspecting;
little rain with malefic aspect in the rainy season soon; with the Moon in Venus's sign and endowed with all such merits...
In the rains, the Moon in the seventh from Venus aspected by benefics, or in the trine or seventh from Saturn, may bring prosperity.
Venus near Mercury makes rain at once; with the Sun between the two, rain is destroyed.
Venus in the five stars from Magha, or in the three of Svati, makes rain; otherwise no rain.
If planets are near the Sun in front or behind, they cause rain; if retrograde, they do not.
Venus on the left side makes rain; if on the south... at risings and settings there is rain; when the Sun enters Ardra,
at the twilights there is increase of crops; at night all prosperity of grain; little rain brings dearness; no rain, wealth of crops.
At the rising of Ardra, if broken, there is rain, without doubt. With the Moon, Jupiter, Mercury or Venus in a centre, danger perishes.
The Sun in Purva Ashadha surrounded by clouds rains from Ardra to Mula, visibly each day.
If there is rain at Pushya, it does not rain in the ten stars after that. With Leo broken, Mars brings rain; with Cancer unbroken likewise.
If Virgo rising is broken, rain is always excellent. Ahirbudhnya is for early crops, Revati for late crops;
Bharani for all crops, Ashvini for the ruin of all. When Venus is in the west in the seventh from Jupiter,
there is much heavy rain in the rainy season, though weak. With the Moon's halo, in the seventh star onward, to the north,
with lightning, croaking frogs, there will be no rain then. When Magha stars bent west stand above the seventh...
those in the south fall; there will be rain soon. Cats scratching the ground with their claws, iron joined...
bridges on a road, boys playing: causes of rain. Broken lines of ants, many fireflies —
climbing trees by snakes, their delight: signs of bad rain. If the sun or moon at rising or setting is discoloured,
or honey-coloured with strong winds, then there will be too much rain. The earth is divided into nine parts like the nine limbs of the east-facing tortoise.
Dividing into nine regions, the circles go around: Antarvedi and Panchala is its navel circle.
In the east, the countries of Magadha and Lata are its face circle; the countries named Stri, Kalinga, Kirata are its arm circle.
Avanti, Dravida, Bhilla are its side circle; Gauda, Konkana, Shalva, Andhra, Pundra are its foot circle.
Sindhu, Kashi, Maharashtra, Saurashtra are the tail circle; Pulinda, China, Yavana, Gurjara are the foot circle.
Kuru, Kashmir, Madreya, Matsya are its side circle; Khasa, Anga, Vanga, Bahlika, Kamboja are the hand circle.
He should place the stars, Krittika and the rest, three by three in order in the nine limbs beginning with the navel; spoiled by malefics, they are spoiled; by benefics, good.
Where images of gods dance, fall, blaze, weep repeatedly, sing, sweat or laugh,
vomit fire or smoke, oil, blood, milk, water, stand face downward, or move from place to place —
such disorders are seen in images; also a Gandharva city (mirage), stars seen by day,
a great meteor fall, rain of wood, grass or blood, a Gandharva-city, smoke from bodies, earthquake by day or night,
sparks without fire, burning without fuel, rainbow at night, a frog on a peak, a white crow,
sparks seen on the bodies of cows, elephants, horses, camels, creatures with two or three heads born in wombs,
in the morning four suns at once afflicting the sun, jackals living in a village, comets seen,
crows crowding at night, doves by day, trees blossoming or fruiting out of season —
the wise prescribe cutting it down and then a peace rite. Such great portents, many, destroy one's place.
